cards.q: Work out 5! (5 factorial).
cards.why: 5! means multiply all the way down to 1: 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120.
cards.hook: n! counts down to 1, multiplying all the way.

cards.q: A café sells 5 different sandwiches and 3 different drinks. How many different meals of one sandwich and one drink can you choose?
cards.why: Every sandwich can go with every drink, so multiply the options: 5 × 3 = 15. Adding (5 + 3 = 8) only counts the items on the menu.
cards.hook: One choice, then another? Multiply the options, don't add.

cards.q: A coin is tossed and a six-sided die is rolled. How many different outcomes (like H5 or T2) are there?
cards.why: Each of the 2 coin results can go with each of the 6 die scores: 2 × 6 = 12 outcomes (H1, H2, …, T6).
cards.hook: Draw it as a table: rows × columns = outcomes.

cards.q: A coin is tossed 3 times. How many different outcomes (like HHT) are there?
cards.why: Each toss has 2 results and every toss goes with every other: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 (HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT).
cards.hook: The same choice made again and again? Multiply it by itself.

cards.q: A spinner has 4 equal sections: red, yellow, blue and green. It is spun twice. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
cards.why: Any of the 4 colours on the 1st spin with any of the 4 on the 2nd, and a colour can come up twice: 4 × 4 = 16.
cards.hook: Two spins of 4: a 4 by 4 table, 16 boxes.

cards.q: A lock code has 3 digits. Each digit can be 0 to 9 and digits may be repeated. How many codes are possible?
cards.why: Repeats are allowed, so each of the 3 places has all 10 digits: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000. (10 × 9 × 8 is for no repeats.)
cards.hook: Repeats allowed: every box keeps all its options.

cards.q: A code has 3 digits, each 0 to 9, and digits may be repeated. How many codes do not contain any zero?
cards.why: No zero leaves 9 options (1 to 9) for every place, and repeats are still allowed: 9 × 9 × 9 = 729.
cards.hook: No zero anywhere: take 0 out of every box, then multiply.

cards.q: In how many different orders can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf?
cards.why: 4 choices for the 1st place, 3 left for the 2nd, 2 for the 3rd, 1 for the last: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 4! = 24.
cards.hook: Each place uses one up: the options go down by 1 each time.

cards.q: 9 different cats are put into 9 separate pens, one cat in each pen. In how many different ways can this be done?
cards.why: 9 cats for the 1st pen, 8 left for the 2nd, and so on down to 1: 9 × 8 × 7 × … × 1 = 9! = 362 880.
cards.hook: n different things into n places: n! (the x! button).

cards.q: How many 3-letter arrangements can be made from the 7 letters of RAINBOW, if each letter is used at most once?
cards.why: 7 letters for the 1st place, 6 left for the 2nd, 5 for the 3rd: 7 × 6 × 5 = 210. Only 3 places, so stop after three.
cards.hook: Only 3 places? Count down 3 times: 7 × 6 × 5.

cards.q: A 4-digit PIN uses the digits 0 to 9, and no digit may be used twice. How many PINs are possible?
cards.why: 10 digits for the 1st place, 9 left for the 2nd, then 8, then 7: 10 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 5040.
cards.hook: No repeats: one fewer option at every step.

cards.q: 8 runners are in a race. In how many different ways can the gold, silver and bronze medals be won?
cards.why: Gold to any of 8, silver to one of the 7 left, bronze to one of 6: 8 × 7 × 6 = 336. Order matters: gold is not silver.
cards.hook: Different prizes? The order matters: count it as an arrangement.

cards.q: The 4 letters of the word FISH are arranged. How many of the arrangements start with F?
cards.why: F is fixed in the 1st place (1 way). The other 3 letters fill the last 3 places: 1 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.
cards.hook: Fill the fussy place first, then count down for the rest.

cards.q: Which of these is a selection, where the order does not matter?
cards.why: Ann, Bob, Cara is the same team as Cara, Ann, Bob, so order doesn't matter. Prizes, PINs and shelves change when you swap the order.
cards.hook: Swap the order: the same thing? Then it is a selection.

cards.q: Which of these is an arrangement, where the order matters?
cards.right: Picking a captain and a vice-captain
wrong: Picking 3 boxes of a password to check
cards.why: Ann captain with Bob vice-captain is not the same as Bob captain with Ann vice-captain: different jobs, so the order matters.
cards.hook: Different jobs or places? Order matters: an arrangement.
keys: different jobs, so the order matters

cards.q: Two of 4 friends (A, B, C and D) are picked to go on a trip together. How many different pairs are possible?
cards.why: List them: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD = 6. AB and BA are the same pair, so 4 × 3 = 12 counts each pair twice.
cards.hook: Order doesn't matter: list in alphabetical order so none repeat.
keys: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD = 6

cards.q: An ice cream van has 7 flavours, 4 toppings, and a choice of a cone or a tub. You pick one flavour, one topping and one container. How many different choices are there?
cards.why: Three choices one after another, so multiply all three: 7 × 4 × 2 = 56. The cone-or-tub choice doubles the 28 flavour-topping pairs.
cards.hook: Every choice gets multiplied in, even a 2-way one.

cards.q: There are 1000 three-digit codes (each digit 0 to 9, repeats allowed), and 729 of them have no zero. How many codes contain at least one zero?
cards.why: "At least one zero" is every code except those with no zero: 1000 − 729 = 271. Counting 3 × 9 × 9 = 243 only finds exactly one zero.
cards.hook: At least one = all of them − none.

cards.q: A club of 5 people picks a chairperson and a secretary (two different people). In how many ways can this be done?
cards.why: 5 choices for chairperson, then 4 left for secretary: 5 × 4 = 20. Ann chair with Bob secretary is not Bob chair with Ann secretary.
cards.hook: Different jobs? Order matters: multiply down, don't halve.

cards.q: A restaurant has 4 starters and 6 main courses. Jack can make 120 different meals of a starter, a main and a dessert. How many desserts are there?
cards.why: Starters × mains × desserts = meals, so 4 × 6 × d = 120. That is 24d = 120, so d = 120 ÷ 24 = 5.
cards.hook: Work back: divide the total by everything you know.

cards.q: Ben picks one subject from each group: Group A has 3, B has 4 and C has 5. One extra subject is added to one group. What is the largest number of choices this can give?
cards.why: Try each: A gives 4 × 4 × 5 = 80, B gives 3 × 5 × 5 = 75, C gives 3 × 4 × 6 = 72. Adding to the smallest group gives the most.
cards.hook: Add the extra one to the smallest group: it multiplies the most.

cards.q: How many arrangements of the 6 letters of PLANET start with P and end with a vowel (A or E)?
cards.why: 1st place: P (1 way). Last place: A or E (2 ways). 4 letters are left for the 4 middle places: 1 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 × 2 = 48.
cards.hook: Fill the fussy places first, then count down for the rest.

cards.q: How many arrangements of the 6 letters of ORANGE start with a vowel (O, A or E)?
cards.why: 1st place: one of the 3 vowels (3 ways). The other 5 letters fill the last 5 places: 3 × 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 360.
cards.hook: Fussy place first: count its options, then the rest count down.

cards.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be made from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, with no digit used twice, if the number must be even?
cards.why: Even means the last digit is 2 or 4 (2 ways). Then 4 digits are left for the 1st place and 3 for the 2nd: 2 × 4 × 3 = 24.
cards.hook: The rule is on the last digit, so fill that place first.

cards.q: A code is 2 letters (A to Z) followed by 3 digits (0 to 9). Letters and digits may repeat. How many codes are possible?
cards.why: Letters: 26 × 26 = 676. Digits: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000. Every letter pair goes with every digit triple: 676 × 1000 = 676 000.
cards.hook: Box by box: write the options in each box, then multiply.

cards.q: A bank asks for 3 of the 5 digits of a PIN (for example the 1st, 3rd and 4th). In how many ways can it choose the 3 positions?
cards.why: Positions 1, 3, 4 are the same choice as 4, 1, 3. In order: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60, but each choice is counted 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 times, so 60 ÷ 6 = 10.
cards.hook: Order doesn't matter? Count in order, then divide by 3 × 2 × 1.

cards.q: Ben picks one subject from each group: 3 languages, 4 sciences and 5 others. How many of his possible choices include French (one of the languages)?
cards.why: French is fixed: 1 way. Then any of 4 sciences and any of 5 others: 1 × 4 × 5 = 20.
cards.hook: A fixed choice counts as 1 option: multiply the rest as usual.

cards.q: How many 4-letter arrangements of the letters of MATHS (no letter used twice) start with M?
cards.why: M is fixed first (1 way). 4 letters are left for the other 3 places: 1 × 4 × 3 × 2 = 24.
cards.hook: A fixed letter is used up: the next place has one fewer to choose from.
